end.summary:
Named common non-metals and identified their states; 6 of 7 responses were unaided correct.
Connected graphite, chlorine, iodine, nitrogen and fertilisers with everyday uses; 2 of 2 responses were unaided correct.
Explained oxygen, carbon and nitrogen as essential to living things; 3 of 3 responses were unaided correct.
Used examples of respiration, burning, plants, proteins and nitrogen conversion; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised classifying non-metals, matching them with everyday uses, and explaining their roles in living things. They used useful examples such as a candle covered by a jar, iodised salt, fertiliser and plant nutrition. No recorded mix-up remained uncorrected. At home, ask them to explain one non-metal’s state, one use and one reason it is important, using a household example.
